# The final case: Freya Bank, credit card statement debt

Freya Bank is fictional. Every customer, card, amount and address in this pack is synthetic.

## When

The case opens Sunday 11 October, 17:00 UTC (20:00 Istanbul). Submissions close Sunday 11 October, 20:00 UTC (23:00 Istanbul).

## The scenario

Freya Bank wants its phone line to answer one of its most common calls with a voice assistant: "how much is my credit card statement debt?". The caller has already passed the bank's phone menu (IVR). The menu has checked who they are and hands the call to the assistant with the customer number. The assistant finds the right card, reads the statement debt in Turkish lira, US dollars, euros and pounds sterling, and says when it is due.

In the same call the customer may want two more things: move their statement date to another week, or get the statement sent to the e-mail address the bank has on file. A customer who wants to pay or who asks for a person is handed to a human agent. The calls are in Turkish.

The bank did not write a clean specification. It sent what it had: an analysis document, the announcements its phone menu reads today, a flow drawing, service descriptions, an integration document, its mails to our team, a list of abbreviations and an FAQ. Deploy it before you run your builder and keep it running until the results are out: our simulated customers reach your mock through the tools in your workflow, so a Worker that is down fails those conversations.

Customer data is in `test-environment/test-customers.json`; amounts and dates come from the service responses there. --- ## Example 1: Single card, debt with a payment below the minimum - **Type:** Happy - **Customer number:** `95004361` - **now:** `2026-10-12T10:30:00+03:00` **Situation:** The customer has a single card. `out/tests.json` yazıldı: 18 test. Ama bu bir taslak; çalıştırmadan önce aşağıdaki boşlukların kapanması lazım.

**İçinde ne var:**
- Örnek konuşmaların altısı da test oldu (T-01 … T-06). Beklenen tutarlar ve tarihler `example-scenarios.md`'den alındı.
- Kalan 12 test bankanın kendi test müşterileriyle kenar durumları deniyor:
  - aynı ad ve aynı son dört hane: son altı haneyi sorma (Ilgaz)
  - ortak ekstreli kartlar, M/C (Sevda)
  - kart listesi 404 ve 500 hatası
  - ürün adında talimat enjeksiyonu (Ceren)
  - e-posta servisi 500 hatası (Cem)
  - ödeme isteyince temsilciye aktarma
  - kızgın arayan: üç sakinleştirme, sonra aktarma
  - üç sessizlik: görüşme biter, ana menü yok
  - kapsam dışı soru
  - adı boş kart (Burak)
  - üç deneme hakkının bitmesi

**Eksik kalanlar:**
- **Takvim Python ile hesaplanmadı.** Bash izni reddedildi. Tüm testler örneklerdeki `now` değerini kullanıyor (12 Ekim 2026). Kendi testlerimde ödeme günü geçmiş ya da ay sonu gibi farklı tarihler yok.
- **Redteam skill'i ve brief'in tamamı okunmadı.** Bash izni reddedildi ve süre yetmedi. Okuduklarım: brief'in başı, örnek konuşmalar, test müşterileri ve 9 Ekim kararlar maili.
- **Ledger anahtarları tahmin.** `statement_sends`, `transfers` içindeki `queue: "agent"` ve `statement_date_changes` mock'tan doğrulanmadı.
- **Kendi testlerimdeki tutarlar `test-customers.json`'dan alınmadı.** Bu yüzden beklentileri çoğunlukla davranış kontrolü olarak yazıldı.

DONE 18 tests

commands.name: core
commands.description: How to build a robust Freya phone agent from a bank's brief. Read first, always. (project)

commands.name: spec-first
commands.description: Turn the brief into an explicit rule list and coverage table before writing the workflow. (project)

commands.name: build-phone-agent
commands.description: Build a Freya phone agent from a bank's brief, test it on the practice customers and fix what fails. Use when asked to build or improve a phone agent from a brief. (project)

commands.name: deep-research
commands.description: Deep research harness — fan-out web searches, fetch sources, adversarially verify claims, synthesize a cited report. (dynamic workflow)

commands.name: design
commands.description: Grant or revoke Claude agent access to your Design projects

commands.name: design-sync
commands.description: Push a React design system to claude.ai/design. This runs a converter that bundles the real component code (from Storybook or a bare package) and uploads it. Use when the user runs /design-sync or says "sync my design system to Claude Design".

commands.name: dataviz
commands.description: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. When the destination is a first-party document connector (host-designated, never self-described) that renders live charts, hand it the rows (inline, or as an uploaded data file the chart cites) rather than a rendered PNG/SVG — a picture of a chart loses hover, data inspection and per-value comments. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".

commands.name: update-config
commands.description: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.

commands.name: verify
commands.description: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes; bootstraps this repo's project verify skill if none exists yet. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.

commands.name: debug
commands.description: Enable debug logging for this session and help diagnose issues

commands.name: code-review
commands.description: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs (plus reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups where the model's review recipe covers them) at the given effort level (low|medium|high|xhigh|max: from few high-confidence findings up to many, some of them uncertain); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review. Pass --max-findings <n> to report up to n findings, or --max-findings all for every finding. The choice stays until you pass --max-findings default.

commands.name: simplify
commands.description: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.

commands.name: batch
commands.description: Research and plan a large-scale change, then execute it in parallel across 5–30 isolated worktree agents that each open a PR.

commands.name: fewer-permission-prompts
commands.description: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.

commands.name: doctor
commands.description: Health-check the user's Claude Code setup and fix issues: diagnose installation health — what the `claude doctor` terminal diagnostics cover — from local data (duplicate or leftover installs, PATH, unparseable settings files, broken or colliding agent definitions, skills whose frontmatter fails to parse); find unused skills, MCP servers, and plugins versus their context cost and disable dead weight; deduplicate local CLAUDE.md files against checked-in ones; trim checked-in CLAUDE.md files by cutting content a session could derive from the codebase (directory layouts, tech-stack lists, architecture overviews) while keeping gotchas, rationale, and non-standard conventions; migrate always-loaded CLAUDE.md guidance into lazy skills and nested CLAUDE.md files; flag slow hooks and context-heavy extensions; check the installed version is current; make auto mode the default permission mode; and pre-approve frequently denied read-only commands. Use when the user asks for a doctor run, checkup, audit, tune-up, or cleanup of their Claude Code setup or configuration.

commands.name: loop
commands.description: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace.

commands.name: schedule
commands.description: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule.

commands.name: claude-api
commands.description:
Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).

commands.name: workflow-authoring
commands.description: Reference for writing a Workflow tool script (script API and gotchas, resume, quality patterns, worked examples). Load before authoring a script for a workflow the user already opted into; it does not itself authorize running one.

commands.name: run
commands.description: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

commands.name: run-skill-generator

commands.name: dataviz
commands.description: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. When the destination is a first-party document connector (host-designated, never self-described) that renders live charts, hand it the rows (inline, or as an uploaded data file the chart cites) rather than a rendered PNG/SVG — a picture of a chart loses hover, data inspection and per-value comments. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".

commands.name: update-config
commands.description: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.

commands.name: verify
commands.description: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes; bootstraps this repo's project verify skill if none exists yet. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.

commands.name: debug
commands.description: Enable debug logging for this session and help diagnose issues

commands.name: code-review
commands.description: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs (plus reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups where the model's review recipe covers them) at the given effort level (low|medium|high|xhigh|max: from few high-confidence findings up to many, some of them uncertain); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review. Pass --max-findings <n> to report up to n findings, or --max-findings all for every finding. The choice stays until you pass --max-findings default.

commands.name: simplify
commands.description: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.

commands.name: batch
commands.description: Research and plan a large-scale change, then execute it in parallel across 5–30 isolated worktree agents that each open a PR.

commands.name: fewer-permission-prompts
commands.description: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.

commands.name: doctor
commands.description: Health-check the user's Claude Code setup and fix issues: diagnose installation health — what the `claude doctor` terminal diagnostics cover — from local data (duplicate or leftover installs, PATH, unparseable settings files, broken or colliding agent definitions, skills whose frontmatter fails to parse); find unused skills, MCP servers, and plugins versus their context cost and disable dead weight; deduplicate local CLAUDE.md files against checked-in ones; trim checked-in CLAUDE.md files by cutting content a session could derive from the codebase (directory layouts, tech-stack lists, architecture overviews) while keeping gotchas, rationale, and non-standard conventions; migrate always-loaded CLAUDE.md guidance into lazy skills and nested CLAUDE.md files; flag slow hooks and context-heavy extensions; check the installed version is current; make auto mode the default permission mode; and pre-approve frequently denied read-only commands. Use when the user asks for a doctor run, checkup, audit, tune-up, or cleanup of their Claude Code setup or configuration.

commands.name: loop
commands.description: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace.

commands.name: schedule
commands.description: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule.

Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review. Pass --max-findings <n> to report up to n findings, or --max-findings all for every finding. The choice stays until you pass --max-findings default.

commands.name: simplify
commands.description: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.

commands.name: batch
commands.description: Research and plan a large-scale change, then execute it in parallel across 5–30 isolated worktree agents that each open a PR.

commands.name: fewer-permission-prompts
commands.description: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.

commands.name: doctor
commands.description: Health-check the user's Claude Code setup and fix issues: diagnose installation health — what the `claude doctor` terminal diagnostics cover — from local data (duplicate or leftover installs, PATH, unparseable settings files, broken or colliding agent definitions, skills whose frontmatter fails to parse); find unused skills, MCP servers, and plugins versus their context cost and disable dead weight; deduplicate local CLAUDE.md files against checked-in ones; trim checked-in CLAUDE.md files by cutting content a session could derive from the codebase (directory layouts, tech-stack lists, architecture overviews) while keeping gotchas, rationale, and non-standard conventions; migrate always-loaded CLAUDE.md guidance into lazy skills and nested CLAUDE.md files; flag slow hooks and context-heavy extensions; check the installed version is current; make auto mode the default permission mode; and pre-approve frequently denied read-only commands. Use when the user asks for a doctor run, checkup, audit, tune-up, or cleanup of their Claude Code setup or configuration.

commands.name: loop
commands.description: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace.

commands.name: schedule
commands.description: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule.

commands.name: claude-api
commands.description:
Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).

commands.name: workflow-authoring
commands.description: Reference for writing a Workflow tool script (script API and gotchas, resume, quality patterns, worked examples). Load before authoring a script for a workflow the user already opted into; it does not itself authorize running one.

commands.name: run
commands.description: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

commands.name: run-skill-generator
commands.description: Author or improve the run-<unit> skill - a per-project skill that tells agents how to build, launch, and drive this project's app. Use when the user asks to set up the project, get it running, write run instructions, or verify build/run steps work from a clean environment.

commands.name: plugin-authoring
commands.description: Make a mod: a change to Claude's own interface or behaviour, such as a live pane or panel, a band above the prompt, a status line, a toast, a slash command, or a hook on tool calls or prompts. Use to make, change or debug a mod or its hooks module.

commands.name: claude.ai Lovable:api_guide (MCP)
commands.description: Guide for calling the Lovable public API directly over HTTPS — authentication, pagination, errors, and a fetch-based quick start for managing and publishing projects

commands.name: claude.ai Lovable:sdk_guide (MCP)
commands.description: Former name of api_guide; returns the same public API guide.

commands.name: claude.ai Lovable:getting_started (MCP)
commands.description: How to build apps with Lovable — covers project creation, effective prompting, integrations, deployment, and iteration workflows

commands.name: claude.ai Vercel:system_instructions (MCP)
commands.description: System instructions for Vercel MCP Server - guides the LLM to prefer MCP tools over CLI when working with Vercel tasks.

commands.name: claude.ai Vercel:explain_vercel_concept (MCP)
commands.description: Answer user questions using search results from Vercel documentation. Use this when you need authoritative information about Vercel features, configuration options, best practices, or troubleshooting guidance. This tool will search the official Vercel documentation and provide accurate, up-to-date information with examples and references.

commands.name: claude.ai Vercel:fix_recent_build (MCP)
commands.description: Analyze and fix issues with the most recent deployment by fetching deployment details and build logs. Use this when your build fails, deployment is stuck, or you need to understand what went wrong. This tool will automatically fetch the latest deployment, analyze its status, retrieve build logs, and provide specific fixes.

commands.name: claude.ai Vercel:analyze_deployment_performance (MCP)
commands.description: Analyze deployment performance metrics and provide optimization recommendations. Use this to identify bottlenecks, slow builds, and opportunities to speed up your deployment pipeline. Perfect for CI/CD optimization and cost reduction.

commands.name: claude.ai Vercel:debug_deployment_issues (MCP)
commands.description: Comprehensive debugging of deployment issues with detailed analysis. Use this when you're experiencing mysterious deployment problems, intermittent failures, or need deep technical analysis of what's going wrong. This tool will perform thorough investigation and provide detailed solutions.

commands.name: claude.ai Vercel:get_project_status (MCP)
commands.description: Get a comprehensive overview of the current project including status, latest deployment, and key metrics. Use this to quickly understand your project's current state, recent activity, and any issues that need attention. Perfect for daily standups, status reports, or when onboarding to a project.

commands.name: claude.ai Vercel:list_team_projects (MCP)
commands.description: List all projects in the current team with their status and latest deployments. Use this to get an overview of all projects your team is working on, identify projects that need attention, or when managing multiple projects. Perfect for team leads, project managers, or when switching between projects.

commands.name: claude.ai Vercel:project_health_check (MCP)
commands.description: Perform a comprehensive health check of the project including deployments, configuration, and potential issues. Use this for regular project maintenance, before major deployments, or when you suspect there might be underlying issues. This tool will provide a detailed health assessment with specific recommendations.

commands.name: claude.ai Vercel:quick_status (MCP)
commands.description: Get a quick overview of the current project status, latest deployment, and any immediate issues. Use this for daily check-ins, quick status updates, or when you need a fast overview without deep analysis. Perfect for busy developers who need instant project insights.

commands.name: claude.ai Vercel:troubleshoot_common_issues (MCP)
commands.description: Help identify and resolve common Vercel deployment and configuration issues. Use this when you're experiencing problems with your deployment, build failures, or configuration issues. This tool will guide you through systematic troubleshooting and provide specific solutions.

commands.name: claude.ai Vercel:optimize_deployment (MCP)
commands.description: Analyze and suggest optimizations for faster builds and better deployment performance. Use this when you want to improve your deployment speed, reduce costs, or enhance your CI/CD pipeline efficiency. This tool will identify bottlenecks and provide specific optimization strategies.

commands.name: claude.ai Vercel:vercel_help (MCP)
commands.description: Get help and guidance on Vercel features, best practices, and configuration options. Use this when you need to learn about Vercel features, understand best practices, or get guidance on implementation. This tool will provide comprehensive help with examples and documentation references.

15	lists), the later or more specific document overrides the earlier one (a memo that changes a policy wins), and the
16	code list fixes the exact outcome / reason / queue strings.
17	
18	Read `docs/workflow-format.md` and `docs/tools-and-code.md` once. The facts below are the ones that cost points.
19	
20	## Platform facts (verified)
21	
22	- Each user turn runs three separate model calls: extraction (node's `extraction_schema`), routing (only transition
23	  descriptions / intents), dialogue (`system_prompt` + `task_message` + history + node `tools`). Routing never reads
24	  `task_message`.
25	- `tools` only on `conversation` nodes; `pre_actions` only on `api_request` / `code` nodes. Anything else is silently dropped.
26	- Tool parameter values: a `default` (literal, or `{{var}}` that is set when the node is entered) is baked and hidden
27	  from the model. A `{{var}}` default whose variable is unset is filled by the model. Never use `const`.
28	- **Every `api_call` body field needs a `default`** (verified on Freya: a field without one is never sent; the agent
29	  looped forever because `field` and `answer` never reached the bank). A model-filled field gets
30	  `"default": "{{<unique name>}}"` whose variable nothing else sets (e.g. `{{vi_answer}}`).
31	- Each `api_call` body field is a leaf under `body.properties.<field>` with its own `default`, `description`, `enum`.
32	- Results: the envelope is `{status, data, message, status_code, header}`; the API body is `data`. Map with `data.` paths.
33	  Flattened keys appear by themselves. For a tool in a conversation node's `tools`: `<tool>_response.data.<field>`,
34	  `<tool>_success_count`, `<tool>_failure_count`. **For a call in `pre_actions` (api_request / code node) every automatic
35	  key is named after the NODE, not the tool**: a node `record` whose pre-action is `create_promise` gives
36	  `record_response.data.ok`, `record_success_count`, `record_failure_count` (verified on Freya). Routes after such a node
37	  must test the node-named keys; a route on `create_promise_response...` never fires there. Safest: in the tool's
38	  `post_process_code`, write your own string flag (`vars['promise_state'] = 'ok'` / `'failed'`) and route on it.
39	- **Lists in results are never mapped to a variable** (verified on Freya: `response_mapping` of `data.products` leaves
40	  `products` unset). Lists only exist as flattened keys, by index: `<prefix>_response.data.products.0.past_due`,
41	  `...products.1.type`. The prefix is the **node name** for a `pre_actions` call (`load_account_response....`) and the
42	  tool name for a tool in `tools`. In code, read products by scanning keys:
43	  `for k, v in vars.items(): m = re.search(r'_response\.data\.products\.(\d+)\.(\w+)$', str(k))` (take the prefix of the most recent account node) and group by index. Never rely on a
44	  mapped list, and never hard-code one prefix.
45	- **Extraction field types:** only `string`, `integer`, `float`, `boolean`, `date`, `datetime`, `enum`, `name`, `phone_number`, `object`. Anything else (`number`, `int`, `text`) is rejected when the workflow is saved. Amounts are `float`.
46	- **A variable declared in any `extraction_schema` can only be written by code with a value that fits that schema**
47	  (verified on Freya: writing `''` or a value outside `enum_values` is rejected with "rejected by schema validation"
48	  and the old value stays). Give code-set flags and counters their own names, never the name of an extracted variable.
49	- **A transition to the node itself is a re-entry** (verified on Freya). `on_enter` runs again (with `on_enter_first_entry_only` the model writes a reply from the `task_message` instead), `<node>.current_turns` resets to 0, and `max_node_turns` restarts. An `always` self-transition plus a `current_turns` or `max_node_turns` limit loops forever: one agent asked the same question 80 times. Never write an `always` self-transition. When no transition matches, the agent stays in the node without re-entry, which is what you want.
50	- `<node>.current_turns` (user turns since the last entry, already 1 when the first user message is routed) and `<node>.total_turns` (whole call, never reset) exist for every node. For "ask at most N times" across re-entries, use `total_turns` or a code counter. `current_turns` only works in a node that is never re-entered.
51	- **Resetting an extracted variable:** code can only write a value that fits the schema. Give every extracted enum a neutral value (`none`), describe it as "the value for the customer's LAST message; `none` if nothing applies", and reset with that value. Never write `''`, never write a value outside `enum_values`, never use `is_set` on an extracted enum. Use one enum per node (`who_greeting`, `who_retry`) so that a value from another node is never read.
52	- Tool parameters are baked when the node is **entered**. A variable that is `""` at entry counts as a value (it is baked empty and hidden from the model). Give model-filled parameters unique names (`cp_amount`, not `amount`) that no code ever writes.
53	- The `tts` of a passthrough `api_request` node is logged **after** its `pre_actions`. If the brief says "goodbye before close_call", say the farewell in a separate passthrough `code` node (`tts` farewell, a one-line snippet) placed before the `close_*` node, and make the `close_*` node `silent`.
54	- Code: import only `json`, `re` and `datetime`. Write only strings and numbers to `vars`. Store lists and dicts as `json.dumps(...)` strings, never as Python lists, dicts, `None` or booleans.
55	- The scoring judge reads the system events (every `function_call_start`, including vetoed or redirected calls, with timestamps). A tool call that should not count must not be made: prefer validating in code before an engine-run call over vetoing inside the call.
56	- Booleans arrive as strings: test `"true"` and `"True"`. Prefer string flags written by code (`ok`, `failed`, ...).
57	- **A failed call (any non-2xx) skips `post_process_code`.** The pre-hook has already run. The model sees only `API request failed: {...}` and no `what_to_do_next`. Freya writes `<t>_response.status = "error"`, `<t>_response.error = "HTTP 500"`, `<t>_response.message`, `<t>_response.status_code`, `<t>_status_code` and increments `<t>_failure_count`. Earlier `<t>_response.data.*` keys are not cleared. So never count failures or write "failed" flags in a post-hook. Route on `<t>_failure_count` (`greater_than 1` → the service-error close) or on `<t>_response.status equals error`, and derive per-item failures in code from what the pre-hook recorded (attempted, and not confirmed by a success post-hook). Put the retry rule in the `task_message` of every node with a write tool: "If a tool result is an error, call the same tool once more with exactly the same values. Never say it worked."
58	- Routing runs again right after a tool result, in the same turn: a transition on a result variable fires at once.
59	- Transitions are checked in order, first match wins; variable conditions need no model call. Top-level condition
60	  groups use `"logic": "or"`; AND is a nested group. Every passthrough node ends with an `always` transition.
61	- Code (`code` node, `pre_process_code`, `post_process_code`): Python with `vars` (and `config` / `result` in hooks).
62	  `json`, `re`, `datetime` work. Never write `{{` or `}}` in code. Wrap everything in `try/except`, write a fallback
63	  for every variable a prompt or route reads. A code node that raises leaves the placeholders unresolved.
64	- `post_process_code` may add `result['data']['what_to_do_next'] = '...'`: the model reads it and acts on it. This is
65	  the fix for "the agent says nothing after a tool call" and "the agent ignores a negative result". Do it on every tool.

Read `docs/workflow-format.md` and `docs/tools-and-code.md` once. The facts below are the ones that cost points.

## Platform facts (verified)

- Each user turn runs three separate model calls: extraction (node's `extraction_schema`), routing (only transition
  descriptions / intents), dialogue (`system_prompt` + `task_message` + history + node `tools`). Routing never reads
  `task_message`.
- `tools` only on `conversation` nodes; `pre_actions` only on `api_request` / `code` nodes. Anything else is silently dropped.
- Tool parameter values: a `default` (literal, or `{{var}}` that is set when the node is entered) is baked and hidden
  from the model. A `{{var}}` default whose variable is unset is filled by the model. Never use `const`.
- **Every `api_call` body field needs a `default`** (verified on Freya: a field without one is never sent; the agent
  looped forever because `field` and `answer` never reached the bank). A model-filled field gets
  `"default": "{{<unique name>}}"` whose variable nothing else sets (e.g. `{{vi_answer}}`).
- Each `api_call` body field is a leaf under `body.properties.<field>` with its own `default`, `description`, `enum`.
- Results: the envelope is `{status, data, message, status_code, header}`; the API body is `data`. Map with `data.` paths.
  Flattened keys appear by themselves. For a tool in a conversation node's `tools`: `<tool>_response.data.<field>`,
  `<tool>_success_count`, `<tool>_failure_count`. **For a call in `pre_actions` (api_request / code node) every automatic
  key is named after the NODE, not the tool**: a node `record` whose pre-action is `create_promise` gives
  `record_response.data.ok`, `record_success_count`, `record_failure_count` (verified on Freya). Routes after such a node
  must test the node-named keys; a route on `create_promise_response...` never fires there. Safest: in the tool's
  `post_process_code`, write your own string flag (`vars['promise_state'] = 'ok'` / `'failed'`) and route on it.
- **Lists in results are never mapped to a variable** (verified on Freya: `response_mapping` of `data.products` leaves
  `products` unset). Lists only exist as flattened keys, by index: `<prefix>_response.data.products.0.past_due`,
  `...products.1.type`. The prefix is the **node name** for a `pre_actions` call (`load_account_response....`) and the
  tool name for a tool in `tools`. In code, read products by scanning keys:
  `for k, v in vars.items(): m = re.search(r'_response\.data\.products\.(\d+)\.(\w+)$', str(k))` (take the prefix of the most recent account node) and group by index. Never rely on a
  mapped list, and never hard-code one prefix.
- **Extraction field types:** only `string`, `integer`, `float`, `boolean`, `date`, `datetime`, `enum`, `name`, `phone_number`, `object`. Anything else (`number`, `int`, `text`) is rejected when the workflow is saved. Amounts are `float`.
- **A variable declared in any `extraction_schema` can only be written by code with a value that fits that schema**
  (verified on Freya: writing `''` or a value outside `enum_values` is rejected with "rejected by schema validation"
  and the old value stays). Give code-set flags and counters their own names, never the name of an extracted variable.
- **A transition to the node itself is a re-entry** (verified on Freya). `on_enter` runs again (with `on_enter_first_entry_only` the model writes a reply from the `task_message` instead), `<node>.current_turns` resets to 0, and `max_node_turns` restarts. An `always` self-transition plus a `current_turns` or `max_node_turns` limit loops forever: one agent asked the same question 80 times. Never write an `always` self-transition. When no transition matches, the agent stays in the node without re-entry, which is what you want.
- `<node>.current_turns` (user turns since the last entry, already 1 when the first user message is routed) and `<node>.total_turns` (whole call, never reset) exist for every node. For "ask at most N times" across re-entries, use `total_turns` or a code counter. `current_turns` only works in a node that is never re-entered.
- **Resetting an extracted variable:** code can only write a value that fits the schema. Give every extracted enum a neutral value (`none`), describe it as "the value for the customer's LAST message; `none` if nothing applies", and reset with that value. Never write `''`, never write a value outside `enum_values`, never use `is_set` on an extracted enum. Use one enum per node (`who_greeting`, `who_retry`) so that a value from another node is never read.
- Tool parameters are baked when the node is **entered**. A variable that is `""` at entry counts as a value (it is baked empty and hidden from the model). Give model-filled parameters unique names (`cp_amount`, not `amount`) that no code ever writes.
- The `tts` of a passthrough `api_request` node is logged **after** its `pre_actions`. If the brief says "goodbye before close_call", say the farewell in a separate passthrough `code` node (`tts` farewell, a one-line snippet) placed before the `close_*` node, and make the `close_*` node `silent`.
- Code: import only `json`, `re` and `datetime`. Write only strings and numbers to `vars`. Store lists and dicts as `json.dumps(...)` strings, never as Python lists, dicts, `None` or booleans.
- The scoring judge reads the system events (every `function_call_start`, including vetoed or redirected calls, with timestamps). A tool call that should not count must not be made: prefer validating in code before an engine-run call over vetoing inside the call.
- Booleans arrive as strings: test `"true"` and `"True"`. Prefer string flags written by code (`ok`, `failed`, ...).
- **A failed call (any non-2xx) skips `post_process_code`.** The pre-hook has already run. The model sees only `API request failed: {...}` and no `what_to_do_next`. Earlier `<t>_response.data.*` keys are not cleared. So never count failures or write "failed" flags in a post-hook. Route on `<t>_failure_count` (`greater_than 1` → the service-error close) or on `<t>_response.status equals error`, and derive per-item failures in code from what the pre-hook recorded (attempted, and not confirmed by a success post-hook). Put the retry rule in the `task_message` of every node with a write tool: "If a tool result is an error, call the same tool once more with exactly the same values. Never say it worked."
- Routing runs again right after a tool result, in the same turn: a transition on a result variable fires at once.
- Transitions are checked in order, first match wins; variable conditions need no model call. Top-level condition
  groups use `"logic": "or"`; AND is a nested group. Every passthrough node ends with an `always` transition.
- Code (`code` node, `pre_process_code`, `post_process_code`): Python with `vars` (and `config` / `result` in hooks).
  `json`, `re`, `datetime` work. Never write `{{` or `}}` in code. Wrap everything in `try/except`, write a fallback

- `post_process_code` may add `result['data']['what_to_do_next'] = '...'`: the model reads it and acts on it. This is
  the fix for "the agent says nothing after a tool call" and "the agent ignores a negative result". Do it on every tool.

  fixed line and run its calls. `end_call` farewell comes from `terminal` (`message_mode` custom/none), not from `on_enter`.
- `max_node_turns` needs a `max_turn_transition`, otherwise it does nothing.
- `context_variables` is dropped on save: put state into prompts with `{{var}}`.
- Leave `agent_config` out. No `null` values anywhere in the JSON.

Handlers for integrations, knowledge search, call transfer and rescheduling also exist. They are not needed here.

`api_call` parameters:

| Parameter | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `url` | Request URL. `{{var}}` works |
| `method` | HTTP method |
| `headers` | Object. Each header is a property with a `default` |
| `body` | Object. Each body field is a property under `body.properties` |
| `connect_retries` | Transport retries. See "Retries and timeouts" |

## How a parameter gets its value

One key decides, per parameter: `default`.

| Declaration | Who supplies the value | Does the model see the parameter |
|---|---|---|
| `default` with a literal, or with a `{{var}}` that has a value | The workflow. The value is **baked** | No |
| `default` with a `{{var}}` that has no value when the node is entered | The model | Yes, named after the variable, with the property's `type`, `description` and `enum` |
| no `default` | The model | Yes |
| `const` | Nobody. `const` does **not** bake | It only constrains the model's own output |

Rules:

- **Use `default` for fixed backend config** such as `url`, `method` and auth headers. At registration the engine moves every `default` into the tool's base config, resolves `{{var}}` from the variable table, and removes the field from the schema the model sees.
- **Never use `const` for a value you want sent.** The engine reads only `default`. A `{{var}}` inside a `const` never resolves. An `api_call` whose `url` is a `const` fails with "URL is required".
- **Baking happens when the node is entered.** A `{{var}}` default is resolved against the variable table at that moment.

The working builder uses this for every tool: `customer_id` has `"default": "{{customer_id}}"` and is baked from a call variable. Every other body field has `"default": "{{<field name>}}"`, where no variable of that name exists, so the model fills it. Verified in a working builder.

Seen in a trial call: the model's arguments are stored as `<tool>_args.<field>` in the variable table, for example `lookup_order_args.order_number`. They were not stored under the bare field name.

Take care that a model-filled field does not share its name with a variable that is already set when the node is entered. The value would be baked and the model would never see the parameter.

### `api_call` body field rules

- Declare each body field as a leaf under `body.properties.<field>`.
- Put the field's `type`, `description` and `enum` on that leaf. Put required fields in `body.required`.
- Give each leaf its own `default`.
- Do not put a field spec at the top level of `parameters.properties` next to a `body.default` template object. The engine looks for the spec at `body.properties.<field>`, does not find it, and the model sees only "Template variable: name". The `enum` and `description` are lost while the call still works.
- A body that exists only as one `body.default` object also shows as an empty form in the dashboard editor. Saving from there removes the tool.

A `code_exec` tool is different: its parameters are true top-level arguments. Declare a model-filled one as a top-level property without `default`.

### When a baked variable has no value

| Field type | Variable unset | Variable is `""` |
|---|---|---|
| Normal field in an engine-run call (`pre_actions`, lifecycle tool) | The field is dropped from the request. No error | The field is sent empty |
| `code` of `code_exec` | The literal text `{{var}}` stays in the Python source and the snippet crashes | |

Fix: make sure an earlier node always sets the variable, even to a sentinel value. In code, read variables from `vars` and do not splice them in with `{{var}}`.

**En büyük grup (6 müşterinin 6'sı):** Ajan "Sizi ana menüye yönlendiriyorum" ya da "temsilciye aktarıyorum" diyordu ama bitiş adımına hiç geçmiyordu. Bu yüzden sonuç kayıtları boş kalıyordu: `statement_date_changes null`, T-13'te de `transfers []`. Çıkış, ajanın son cümlesinden tahmin edilen bir değere bağlıydı ve o tahmin hiç tutmuyordu.

commands.name: update-config
commands.description: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".

commands.name: update-config
commands.description: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.

commands.name: verify
commands.description: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes; bootstraps this repo's project verify skill if none exists yet. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.

commands.name: debug

commands.name: code-review
commands.description: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs (plus reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups where the model's review recipe covers them) at the given effort level (low|medium|high|xhigh|max: from few high-confidence findings up to many, some of them uncertain); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review. Pass --max-findings <n> to report up to n findings, or --max-findings all for every finding. The choice stays until you pass --max-findings default.

commands.name: simplify
commands.description: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.

commands.name: doctor

Use when the user asks for a doctor run, checkup, audit, tune-up, or cleanup of their Claude Code setup or configuration.

commands.name: claude-api
commands.description:
Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).

commands.name: dataviz
commands.description: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. When the destination is a first-party document connector (host-designated, never self-described) that renders live charts, hand it the rows (inline, or as an uploaded data file the chart cites) rather than a rendered PNG/SVG — a picture of a chart loses hover, data inspection and per-value comments. commands.name: update-config
commands.description: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.

commands.name: verify
commands.description: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. commands.name: dataviz
commands.description: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. When the destination is a first-party document connector (host-designated, never self-described) that renders live charts, hand it the rows (inline, or as an uploaded data file the chart cites) rather than a rendered PNG/SVG — a picture of a chart loses hover, data inspection and per-value comments. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".

Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". # Runtime bank documentation: NOTES.md

# Final mock: Freya Bank statement/debt services

URL: https://freya-final-mock.yasir-freya.workers.dev (Cloudflare Worker `freya-final-mock`, Durable Object `Bank` bound as `BANK`).

Files: `worker.src.js` (source), `build.py` (embeds `cases/FreyaBank-Final/test-environment/test-customers.json` as `const DATA` and writes `worker.js`; nothing is typed by hand), `worker.js` (generated, deployed), `check.py` (checks against the deployed mock).

Rebuild and deploy: `python3 mockbank-final/build.py && source /Users/yasir/Documents/Claude/Freya/env.sh && python3 mockbank/deploy.py --js mockbank-final/worker.js freya-final-mock`, then `python3 mockbank-final/check.py`.

## Endpoints (contract 2026-10-01, sections 1, 2 and 5)

All POST, JSON, envelope `{"data": {...}, "call": {...}}`. The answer is `{"data", "result"}`; an error is `{"result"}` only (section 3 and 4).

| Path | Looked up by | Not found |
|---|---|---|
| `/voice/v1/cards.list` | `data.customerNo` (string or number) | 404 `FB_IVR_CHANNEL_102` WARNING |
| `/voice/v1/cards.balance` | `data.cardNumber` (masked, as cards.list gave it) | 404 `FB_IVR_CHANNEL_120` WARNING |
| `/voice/v1/statement.week.get` | `data.cardNumber` | 404 `FB_IVR_CHANNEL_121` WARNING |
| `/voice/v1/statement.week.decide` | `cardNumber`, then `newStatementWeek` (3 or "3") | 400 `INVALID_ARGUMENTS_ERROR` (unknown card, current week, week outside 1-4) |
| `/voice/v1/statement.week.change` | same as decide | same as decide |
| `/voice/v1/contact.email.get` | `data.customerNo`; `intAddressInfoType` does not change the answer | 400 `INVALID_ARGUMENTS_ERROR` |
| `/voice/v1/statement.pdf.send` | `data.customerNo` | 404 `FB_IVR_CHANNEL_107` "Pdf dokümanı bulunamadı" |
| `/oauth2/token` | form or anything | always 200 `{access_token, token_type: "Bearer", expires_in: 1800}` |

- For test customers the mock returns the listed body and HTTP status exactly, with the listed `guid`s. This includes the listed 500s (97073972 cards.list, 92335586 contact.email.get, 94835408 statement.week.get, 94339861 decide), the 404s (93821776 cards.list, 93635512 pdf.send) and the 12 s `delaySeconds` on 94907600's cards.balance. The delay runs in the Worker, not in the Durable Object, and the field is not put in the body.
- Required fields that are missing or empty give 400 `INVALID_ARGUMENTS_ERROR` (type ERROR) and a message that names the field, e.g. `card number cannot be empty`, `intAddressInfoType cannot be empty`, `newStatementWeek cannot be empty`, `statementDay cannot be empty`, `emailAddress cannot be empty`. The required fields are customerNo (cards.list, contact.email.get, pdf.send); cardNumber (card services, pdf.send); newStatementWeek and statementDay (decide, change); intAddressInfoType; and currencyType, statementDate and emailAddress (pdf.send). Contract section 4 and 5.
- Error bodies are built like the contract examples: `returnCode`=`code`, `messageText`=`message`, a new 32-hex `guid` (also in `details.guid`), and `errorOrigin` `ivr-gateway-test:ivr-channel-v0`. If a handler crashes, the mock answers 500 `FBE00099` "Teknik hata: ABORTED: ".
- Invalid JSON gives a 400. GET on a service gives a 405.

## Auth

The token endpoint issues a token. The services do **not** check the token or the headers (contract section 2: "token and headers are not checked there", section 6, test-customers.md). A request without a token or with a bogus one gets the same answer.

## How customers are found

These are the lookup keys from test-customers.md. Card numbers are unique across customers, so a card call finds its owner without a customerNo. The balance-format number (`5400********1234`) does not match any card and gives a 404, because the contract says to send the number exactly as cards.list returned it. A literal `{{customerNumber}}` or `{{...}}` card number, which the Freya panel's "Test API Request" can send, is answered as customer 90000001 or card 540000******1234 (cloudflare-mock/README).

## State, sessions and ledger keys (our practice routes, not in the contract)

- `POST /v1/practice/sessions {"case": "<customerNo or registered case id>", "now"?}` returns `{ok, variables: {customerNumber, now, customer_id}}`. The default `now` is `2026-10-12T10:30:00+03:00` (example-scenarios.md).
- `GET /v1/practice/ledger/<customer_id>` returns the ledger. `POST /v1/practice/end {"customer_id"}` stops routing calls to that session.
- `POST /v1/practice/register {"cases": [{id, variables: {customerNumber, now}, services?, faults?}]}`. `services` uses the test-customers.json shape and is required when customerNumber is not a built-in test customer. `faults` is `[{"tool": "cards.balance", "fail_first_n": 1, "http"?: 401}]` and gives a 500 `FBE00099` (or a 401) on the first n calls in that session.
- The services carry no call id, only customerNo or cardNumber. A call therefore goes to the **latest practice session opened for that customer in the last 30 minutes**. Otherwise it goes to `live:<customerNo>` (the organisers' runs; the last 300 calls are kept). A new session starts with an empty ledger, so two runs one after the other do not see each other's records. Two parallel self-test runs of the *same* customer would share one ledger (limitation); different customers in parallel are fine.
- **Changes never alter the answers.** The test data has fixed answers per card and week (contract section 6, test-customers.md). After a `statement.week.change`, `statement.week.get` still returns the listed body. The change is only recorded.
- Ledger keys:
  - `calls`: `[{n, tool, args (the data object), status, result}]` for every call, errors included.
  - `statement_week_changes`: `[{cardNumber, newStatementWeek, statementDay}]` for each successful (200) change. `cardNumber` is a string; `newStatementWeek` and `statementDay` are JSON numbers (the recorder converts them with `Number`). `statementDay` is the submitted current day, not the new day returned in the preview.
  - `statement_week_previews`: the same shape, for each successful decide.
  - `statement_pdf_sends`: `[{customerNo, cardNumber, currencyType, statementDate, emailAddress}]` for each successful send; all five fields are strings. The address is recorded as sent and is not checked (contract 5.7), so tests can assert that only the registered address was used.
  - `contact_lookups`: `[{customerNo, intAddressInfoType}]`.
  - Practice keys kept for selftest: `outcome`/`reason`: null, `promises`, `notes`, `callbacks` and `transfers`: [] (the contract has no closing, transfer or promise service; the hand-over is on the platform side), and `identity`: {} (the IVR has already identified the caller). Also `case`, `customerNo`, `now`, `attempts`.

## Assumptions

1. Token not enforced, and `call`/`aiFlow` are ignored (contract sections 2 and 6).
2. Enum values are not validated: `currencyType`, `intAddressInfoType` and the value of `statementDay`. test-customers.md says pdf.send has "one answer per customer" and that `intAddressInfoType` doesn't change the answer. Whatever was sent is recorded, so tests can check it.
3. pdf.send does not check that the card or statementDate belongs to the customer (lookup by customerNo only, test-customers.md).
4. A flat body (fields at the top level, no `data`) is accepted as `data`. This is leniency only, so a slightly wrong tool still works.
5. The yearly limit on week changes is not enforced: the contract has no such flag (open point 3), and Kerem says the rule lives in the card system. The decisions recap (9 Oct) changes only agent behaviour: the card number never read beyond the last 4, and the last-six or full-number steps. The mock follows the test environment (masked numbers).
6. The 404 texts for 120 and 121 are our own wording; the contract says only the code matters.

content.text:
I fixed the two failures that were real agent faults by editing `out/agent.workflow.json` directly (there's no generator script). The contract check now reports 0 errors and 0 warnings. I haven't re-run the four failing customers, so neither fix is tested yet.

- **S-pieces-T-02 (statement week change never made):** the customer said "week 3" in the same sentence as the request, before the week-question node started. That node's choice field only read the customer's last message, so their "Evet" ("yes") gave no week number, and the agent made up an "I can't complete it" reply. The field's description now tells it to use a week mentioned earlier in the call when the customer then says yes. The route from there is unchanged: preview, confirmation, then the change call. This is a prompt-level fix, not a route.
- **T-04 (last month's statement sent silently):** the email confirmation question now always begins "Yalnızca en son dönem ekstrenizi gönderebiliyorum." ("I can only send your latest statement"). It is fixed spoken text, so it is said every time, not left to the model.
- **T-03 and T-05:** I made no changes. In both, the test customer never asked for the behaviour being checked: T-03 never asks for a repeat, and T-05 never asks for a spouse's card. The agent didn't get a chance to fail, so these need fixing in the test customers, not the agent.

Rewriting the JSON also re-indented the whole file, so a diff against an earlier copy will show more lines than the two edits.

DONE

Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).

commands.name: workflow-authoring
commands.description: Reference for writing a Workflow tool script (script API and gotchas, resume, quality patterns, worked examples). Load before authoring a script for a workflow the user already opted into; it does not itself authorize running one.

commands.name: run
commands.description: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

commands.name: run-skill-generator
commands.description: Author or improve the run-<unit> skill - a per-project skill that tells agents how to build, launch, and drive this project's app. Use when the user asks to set up the project, get it running, write run instructions, or verify build/run steps work from a clean environment.

commands.name: plugin-authoring
commands.description: Make a mod: a change to Claude's own interface or behaviour, such as a live pane or panel, a band above the prompt, a status line, a toast, a slash command, or a hook on tool calls or prompts. Use to make, change or debug a mod or its hooks module.

commands.name: claude.ai Meta Ads:analyze_ads_performance (MCP)
commands.description: A 60-day performance review of the selected ad account: what's working, what's not, notable week-over-week movements, and the highest-impact next action.

commands.name: claude.ai Lovable:api_guide (MCP)
commands.description: Guide for calling the Lovable public API directly over HTTPS — authentication, pagination, errors, and a fetch-based quick start for managing and publishing projects

commands.name: claude.ai Lovable:sdk_guide (MCP)
commands.description: Former name of api_guide; returns the same public API guide.

commands.name: claude.ai Lovable:getting_started (MCP)
commands.description: How to build apps with Lovable — covers project creation, effective prompting, integrations, deployment, and iteration workflows

commands.name: claude.ai Vercel:system_instructions (MCP)
commands.description: System instructions for Vercel MCP Server - guides the LLM to prefer MCP tools over CLI when working with Vercel tasks.

commands.name: claude.ai Vercel:explain_vercel_concept (MCP)
commands.description: Answer user questions using search results from Vercel documentation. Use this when you need authoritative information about Vercel features, configuration options, best practices, or troubleshooting guidance. This tool will search the official Vercel documentation and provide accurate, up-to-date information with examples and references.

commands.name: claude.ai Vercel:fix_recent_build (MCP)
commands.description: Analyze and fix issues with the most recent deployment by fetching deployment details and build logs. Use this when your build fails, deployment is stuck, or you need to understand what went wrong. This tool will automatically fetch the latest deployment, analyze its status, retrieve build logs, and provide specific fixes.

commands.name: claude.ai Vercel:analyze_deployment_performance (MCP)
commands.description: Analyze deployment performance metrics and provide optimization recommendations. Use this to identify bottlenecks, slow builds, and opportunities to speed up your deployment pipeline. Perfect for CI/CD optimization and cost reduction.

commands.name: claude.ai Vercel:debug_deployment_issues (MCP)
commands.description: Comprehensive debugging of deployment issues with detailed analysis. Use this when you're experiencing mysterious deployment problems, intermittent failures, or need deep technical analysis of what's going wrong. This tool will perform thorough investigation and provide detailed solutions.

commands.name: claude.ai Vercel:get_project_status (MCP)
commands.description: Get a comprehensive overview of the current project including status, latest deployment, and key metrics. Use this to quickly understand your project's current state, recent activity, and any issues that need attention. Perfect for daily standups, status reports, or when onboarding to a project.

commands.name: claude.ai Vercel:list_team_projects (MCP)
commands.description: List all projects in the current team with their status and latest deployments. Use this to get an overview of all projects your team is working on, identify projects that need attention, or when managing multiple projects. Perfect for team leads, project managers, or when switching between projects.

commands.name: claude.ai Vercel:project_health_check (MCP)
commands.description: Perform a comprehensive health check of the project including deployments, configuration, and potential issues. Use this for regular project maintenance, before major deployments, or when you suspect there might be underlying issues. This tool will provide a detailed health assessment with specific recommendations.

commands.name: claude.ai Vercel:quick_status (MCP)
commands.description: Get a quick overview of the current project status, latest deployment, and any immediate issues. Use this for daily check-ins, quick status updates, or when you need a fast overview without deep analysis. Perfect for busy developers who need instant project insights.

commands.name: claude.ai Vercel:troubleshoot_common_issues (MCP)
commands.description: Help identify and resolve common Vercel deployment and configuration issues. Use this when you're experiencing problems with your deployment, build failures, or configuration issues. This tool will guide you through systematic troubleshooting and provide specific solutions.

commands.name: claude.ai Vercel:optimize_deployment (MCP)
commands.description: Analyze and suggest optimizations for faster builds and better deployment performance. Use this when you want to improve your deployment speed, reduce costs, or enhance your CI/CD pipeline efficiency. This tool will identify bottlenecks and provide specific optimization strategies.

commands.name: claude.ai Vercel:vercel_help (MCP)
commands.description: Get help and guidance on Vercel features, best practices, and configuration options. Use this when you need to learn about Vercel features, understand best practices, or get guidance on implementation. This tool will provide comprehensive help with examples and documentation references.

commands.name: claude.ai Vercel:purchase_vercel_domain (MCP)
commands.description: Guide domain registration with a price quote, required disclosures, and explicit approval before charging.

commands.name: claude.ai higgsfield:reset-credits (MCP)
commands.description: Open the Credit Reset offer. Does not claim credits or change the subscription.

I fixed four of the failures in `out/agent.workflow.json`. There was no generator script, so I edited the JSON directly. The contract check now reports 0 errors and 0 warnings. I haven't re-run the test customers, so none of these fixes is confirmed yet.

1. **Due date said without the year (T-01, T-02).** The code that builds the debt reading was cutting the year off the due date to add a Turkish suffix. It now says the full date, e.g. "15 Ekim 2026", with no suffix. This applies to every customer.
2. **Week choices not offered (T-02).** The week options ("ayın 1., 3. ya da 4. haftası…") are now built in code from the customer's current week and spoken right after the week information. Before, the agent only asked "değiştirmek ister misiniz?".
3. **Week change never carried out (S-pieces-T-02).** The customer had already said "3. hafta" while the debt was being read, and the agent lost it. The debt-reading step and the offer step now listen for a week number, and the week-building code reads it. If it's a valid choice, the call goes straight to the preview step, which reads the week information plus the new statement and due dates, then asks for confirmation. The change is made only after the customer confirms.
4. **Last month's statement requested (T-04).** The email question now starts with "Yalnızca son ekstrenizi gönderebilirim." So the customer hears that only the latest statement can be sent.

**T-03 and T-05 not changed:** the test customer never asked for the thing being checked: a repeat in T-03, a spouse card in T-05. Everything else in those calls passed, so I left the agent as it was.

No test id, customer id, fixture date or preferred week is hardcoded.

I fixed four of the failures in `out/agent.workflow.json`. There was no generator script, so I edited the JSON directly. The contract check now reports 0 errors and 0 warnings. I haven't re-run the test customers, so none of these fixes is confirmed yet.

1. **Due date said without the year (T-01, T-02).** The code that builds the debt reading was cutting the year off the due date to add a Turkish suffix. It now says the full date, e.g. "15 Ekim 2026", with no suffix. This applies to every customer.
2. **Week choices not offered (T-02).** The week options ("ayın 1., 3. ya da 4. haftası…") are now built in code from the customer's current week and spoken right after the week information. Before, the agent only asked "değiştirmek ister misiniz?".
3. **Week change never carried out (S-pieces-T-02).** The customer had already said "3. hafta" while the debt was being read, and the agent lost it. The debt-reading step and the offer step now listen for a week number, and the week-building code reads it. If it's a valid choice, the call goes straight to the preview step, which reads the week information plus the new statement and due dates, then asks for confirmation. The change is made only after the customer confirms.
4. **Last month's statement requested (T-04).** The email question now starts with "Yalnızca son ekstrenizi gönderebilirim." So the customer hears that only the latest statement can be sent.

**T-03 and T-05 not changed:** the test customer never asked for the thing being checked: a repeat in T-03, a spouse card in T-05. Everything else in those calls passed, so I left the agent as it was.

No test id, customer id, fixture date or preferred week is hardcoded.

DONE.

### 3.3 When the answer doesn't settle the card

- **Name half-said or described** (a colour, "the travel one", only the brand): if it fits several cards, read back just those names; if it fits none, read all the names again, and that uses up one try. A card we don't have on the list at all (another bank's, one that's been closed): tell them there's no card under that name and read the eligible ones again.
- **"All of them, please":** we can't, the balance service works one card at a time. Put the selection question from 3.1 again; this costs a try just like an answer we can't use, and when the three are gone: “Size şu anda yardımcı olamıyorum. Sizi ana menüye aktarıyorum.”
- **Digits:** however the caller says them (digit by digit, in pairs, as one big number), we turn them into the four digits, e.g. 4253, and go straight to that card's debt. Wrong digits or "I don't have the card on me": ask again (for the digits, or for the card name if they can't give digits), three tries, then the main menu. If they read out the whole card number we find the card from it. Whatever they said, four digits, six or all sixteen, the assistant does not say it back to them.
- **Switching:** a caller who picks a card and then wants a different one goes back to selection. After a reading, a question about another of their cards also goes back to selection, and we read that second card.
- **Supplementary card only** (`isMainCard` false): tell them there is no eligible card for this and ask them to choose a different one.
- **No product name from the service:** the card is introduced by its last four only, “Sonu 4253 ile biten kartınıza ait …”

## 4. Reading the debt

### 4.1 Order

Kerem and I agreed this order on 7 Oct; it is the order for every reading:

1. Card introduction and the statement closing date
2. Turkish Lira debt
3. Dollar, then Euro, then İngiliz Sterlini debts
